The smallest positive real number \(C\) is the operator norm (spectral norm) of the matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix}\), which is the square root of the largest eigenvalue of \(A^T A\).

Compute \(A^T A\):
\[
A^T A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 6 \\ 6 & 13 \end{pmatrix}.
\]
The eigenvalues satisfy \(\det(A^T A - \lambda I) = 0\):
\[
(4-\lambda)(13-\lambda) - 36 = \lambda^2 - 17\lambda + 16 = 0,
\]
giving \(\lambda = 16\) and \(\lambda = 1\). The singular values are \(\sqrt{16}=4\) and \(\sqrt{1}=1\). The maximum singular value is \(4\), so the smallest such \(C\) is \(4\).

Answer: 4
